Rashi on Chullin 67b:10:1.hebrew: מינה גבלי - לשון גדלי. מן הבהמה עצמה הן גדלין, ולאו שרץ הארץ נינהו:
Rashi on Chullin 67b:10:1.english: Minah gavlei - [This is an] expression [meaning] "they grow" [gadlei]. They grow from the animal itself, and are not a creeping thing of the earth:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:11:1.hebrew: מינם ניים ועיילי ליה באוסייה - כשהבהמה ישנה, נכנסים בחוטמה, ומשם לקנה, ריאה וכבד, הלכך לא משתכחי דרך בית הרעי:
Rashi on Chullin 67b:11:1.english: It sleeps, and they enter it through its snout - When the animal sleeps, [the worms] enter through its snout, and from there [they travel] to the windpipe, lung, and liver; therefore, they are not found [passing] through the digestive tract:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:11:2.hebrew: דרני - תולעים הנמצאים בין עור לבשר כשמפשיטין הבהמה, ובלע"ז גרביליי"ש:
Rashi on Chullin 67b:11:2.english: Deranei - [These are] worms that are found between the skin and the flesh when they skin the animal, and in Old French, gravelles:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:11:3.english: [They] are forbidden - and the reason is explained ahead:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:11:4.english: [Worms] of fish are permitted - and the reason is as Ravina explains:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:12:1.hebrew: אבלע לי - דרני דכוורי, בתוך הדגים תני אותם, שלא אראה ואקוץ בם:
Rashi on Chullin 67b:12:1.english: Conceal [them] for me - [The worms] of fish, place them inside the fish, so that I will not see [them] and be disgusted by them:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:13:1.hebrew: בשחיטה משתריא - ואלו שגדלו בתוכה עד שלא נשחטה, באו מאיסור אבר מן החי, ושחיטת הבהמה לא אהניא לדידהו, שהרי יש להם חיות לעצמן. ואע"ג דשליל מותר בשחיטת אמו, מכל בבהמה תאכלו נפקא לן לקמן, אבל הכא באיסורייהו קיימי:
Rashi on Chullin 67b:13:1.english: [An animal] is rendered permitted by slaughter - And these [worms] that grew inside it before it was slaughtered came from the prohibition of a limb from a living animal, and the slaughter of the animal is not effective for them, since they have life of their own. And even though a fetus is permitted through the slaughter of its mother, we derive [that] later on from [the verse], "anything within an animal you may eat," but here they remain in their forbidden state:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:14:1.hebrew: שילשול - תולעת ארוכה כנחש הן, והן הנמצאין באשפה:
Rashi on Chullin 67b:14:1.english: Shilshul [earthworm] - They are a long worm like a snake, and they are [the ones] found in a refuse heap:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:15:1.english: [It] is a kosher fish - for it has fins and scales, as [the baraita] explains:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:15:2.english: Strong shields - [This means] strength of shields:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:15:3.english: These are scales - [which are] closed and sealed tightly upon it.

Rashi on Chullin 67b:15:4.english: Sharpest potsherds are under him - sharp [edges] of potsherds:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:15:5.hebrew: אלו סנפירים - שחדודים ומחתכין כחרסין, ובהן הוא בוקע את המים בחודן, שלא יעכבוהו בפריחתו. פשטיה דקרא, לשון מורי: "תחתיו חדודי חרס" — במקומו זהרורי שמש:
Rashi on Chullin 67b:15:5.english: These are fins - which are sharp and cut like potsherds, and with them it cleaves the water with their sharp edge, so that [the water] does not impede it in its swimming. The plain meaning of the verse, [in] the words of my teacher: "*Tachtav chadudei cheres*" — [meaning,] in its place [beneath it, there are] rays of the sun:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:1:1.hebrew: באביה - בעודה מחוברת, שרץ הארץ היא ואסורה התולעת לאכול, דכיון דמהלכת בתוך הקישות והיא מחוברת בקרקע, הוי כמהלכת על גבי קרקע; אבל התליעה לאחר מכאן, מותרת עד שתצא לאויר:
Rashi on Chullin 67b:1:1.english: While attached [to the ground] - While it is still attached, it is [considered] a swarming thing of the earth, and the worm is forbidden to eat; for since it moves inside the cucumber while [the cucumber] is attached to the ground, it is like [one] moving upon the ground. However, [if] it became wormy afterward, it is permitted until it emerges into the open air:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:2:1.hebrew: להוציא זיזין שבעדשים - דמותרים, דלאו על הארץ שורצין, אלא בתוך העדשה:
Rashi on Chullin 67b:2:1.english: To exclude zizin that are in lentils - [meaning] that they are permitted, since they do not swarm upon the earth, but rather inside the lentil:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:2:2.hebrew: זיזין - כוצונ"ש, וכמין יתושין הן, אלא שבעדשים זיזין שמן:
Rashi on Chullin 67b:2:2.english: Zizin - [In Old French:] coçons [weevils], and they are a type of mosquito, except that [those] in lentils are called zizin:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:2:3.hebrew: כליסין - מין קטנית, צידרא"ש בלע"ז:
Rashi on Chullin 67b:2:3.english: Kelisin - A type of legume, tsidras [chickpeas] in Old French:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:2:4.english: And it is taught [in] another [baraita], “every” [serves] to include - [meaning] that they are prohibited:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:3:1.english: In the fruit - [meaning] that the dates themselves became wormy:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:3:2.english: And this [one refers to fruit] while it is attached [to the ground] - they are forbidden, and [this is] a support for Shmuel:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:4:1.hebrew: אידי ואידי באביה - כלומר: הא דשרי נמי באביה, דכל כמה דלא נפקא לאויר, לאו שרץ הארץ היא, ולא תסייעיה:
Rashi on Chullin 67b:4:1.english: Both this and that [refer to when it is] attached [to the ground] - That is to say, the [baraita] that permits [the insect] is also [speaking of] when it is attached [to the ground], for as long as it has not emerged into the air, it is not [considered] a creeping thing of the earth, and it does not support him [Shmuel].

Rashi on Chullin 67b:6:1.hebrew: פירשה ומתה - המתלעת לאחר תלישתה, דשריא לדברי הכל, פירשה מתוך הפרי לארץ ולא ריחשה, שמתה מיד בנפילתה:
Rashi on Chullin 67b:6:1.english: [If] it emerged and died - [A worm] that developed after its [the fruit's] detachment, which is permitted according to all opinions, emerged from inside the fruit onto the ground, but did not creep, as it died immediately upon falling:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:6:2.hebrew: מהו - מי אמרי': כיון דלא הלכה, לאו "שורץ על הארץ" הוא, או דלמא לא בעינן שריצה? שורץ היינו רוחש ומנענע:
Rashi on Chullin 67b:6:2.english: What is [the halakha] - Do we say: since it did not walk, it is not [considered] "swarming upon the earth," or perhaps we do not require swarming? "Swarming" means creeping and moving:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:6:3.hebrew: מקצתה מהו - מי הויא ככולה, או דלמא בעינן כולה:
Rashi on Chullin 67b:6:3.english: [If] part of it [emerged], what is [the halakha] - Is it [considered] like all of it, or perhaps we require all of it [to emerge]:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:6:4.hebrew: לאויר העולם - פירשה מן הפרי תלוש לאויר, וקודם שהגיע לארץ קלטה בפיו לבולעה. אם תימצי לומר פירשה ומתה מותרת משום דאינה ראויה לרחוש, אבל חיה דראויה לרחוש — לא:
Rashi on Chullin 67b:6:4.english: Into the air of the world - It emerged from the detached fruit into the air, and before it reached the ground, he caught it in his mouth to swallow it. If you conclude to say [that if] it emerged and died it is permitted because it is not fit to crawl, but [if it is] alive, since it is fit to crawl, [it is] not [permitted]:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:7:1.hebrew: לגג תמרה מהו - מתוכה פירשה לגגה, מי אמרי' היינו רביתיה, או דלמא כשורץ על גבי דבר אחר דמי:
Rashi on Chullin 67b:7:1.english: Onto the roof of a date, what is [the law]? - [If the worm] emerged from within it onto its roof, do we say this is its [normal manner of] growth, or perhaps it is like [one] swarming upon another thing:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:7:2.hebrew: לגג גרעינתה מהו - אם תמצי לומר לגג תמרה כדבר אחר הוא, גג גרעינתה מהו? כל תולעים מגרעיני הפרי הן גדלים:
Rashi on Chullin 67b:7:2.english: Onto the roof of its pit, what is [the law] - If you say [that climbing] onto the roof of the date is [considered] like [moving onto] another entity, what is [the law regarding] the roof of its pit? All worms grow from the pits of the fruit:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:7:3.hebrew: מתמרה לתמרה מהו - ולא שרץ על גבה, אלא מזו על זו: מי אמרי', כיון דלאו היינו אמה, "שורץ" קרינא ביה, או דלמא אויר העולם בעינן? וכולהו בתלושין בעי להו:
Rashi on Chullin 67b:7:3.english: From a date to a date, what is [the halakha]? - And it did not creep upon its [own] surface, rather [it moved] from this [date] onto that [date]: do we say that since this is not its mother [fruit], we apply to it [the term] "creeping," or perhaps we require [exposure to] the air of the world? And he raises all of these [dilemmas] regarding detached [dates]:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:8:1.english: Kukeyanei - Worms in the liver and in the lung:

Rashi on Chullin 67b:9:1.hebrew: מעלמא אתו - שבלעתן הבהמה עם האוכלים, ותחלתן שרצו על הארץ:
Rashi on Chullin 67b:9:1.english: They came from the world [outside] - [Meaning] that the animal swallowed them with the food, and originally they crept upon the earth:

Tosafot on Chullin 67b:12:1.hebrew: לרבות דרנים שבבהמה - וא"ת, ותיפוק ליה דאסירי, מידי דהוה אשוחט הבהמה ומצא בה דמות יונה, דאסירא משום דליתיה לא בפרסה ולא בפרסות? ויש לומר, דשאני עובר, משום דמקרא ד"וכל בהמה" אישתרי, ולית ליה למשרי אלא היכא דאיכא פרסות, דבקרא ד"וכל בהמה" כתיב "פרסה"; אבל דרנים שבבהמה נבראין מן הבשר עצמה, והוה אמרינן דחשיבי כבשר. ולא דמי לחותך מן הטחול ומן הכליות, דהתם איכא חסרון, ואסירי לקמן (חולין סט.) מ"אותה" — שלמה ולא חסרה, אבל הכא לא נחסר דבר:
Tosafot on Chullin 67b:12:1.english: To include worms that are in animals - And if you ask: Let it be derived that they are forbidden, just like [the case of] one who slaughters an animal and finds inside it [a fetus in] the likeness of a dove, which is forbidden because it has neither a hoof nor cloven hooves? One can say [in answer] that a fetus is different, because it was permitted from the verse "and every animal," and it is only permitted where there are hooves, for in the verse "and every animal" it is written "hoof." However, worms in an animal are generated from the meat itself, and we would have said that they are considered like meat. And it is not comparable to one who cuts [a piece] from the spleen or from the kidneys, for there, there is a deficiency, and they are forbidden below (Chullin 69a) from [the word] "it" (otah) — whole and not lacking — whereas here, nothing is lacking:

Tosafot on Chullin 67b:5:1.hebrew: דיקא נמי דקתני תולעת שבעיקרי זיתים - מכאן מדקדק ר"ת ורבינו נתנאל וריב"א, דאין הלכה כשמואל דאמר "קישות שהתליעה באביה אסורה". ובהלכות גדולות ובשאלתות דרב אחאי פוסק כשמואל, מדאמר רב פפא לעיל בפירקין (חולין דף נח.): ש"מ מדרב הונא הא דאמר שמואל "קישות שהתליעה באביה אסורה", הני תמרי דכדא בתר תריסר ירחי שרי. אע"פ שהש"ס עושה כאן דיוק מן הברייתא דלא כשמואל, היינו לכאורה; אבל לשמואל נמי יש ליישב ולפרש, ד"תולעת שבעיקרי זיתים" היינו שבזיתים בעודן מחוברין בעיקרן. ומיהו אפי' לשמואל אין לאסור אותן פולין שקורין פואי"ש בלע"ז, וחימצי שקורין שאווי"ם, כשנמצאין בתוכן כגון יבחושין — ובתחלת תולדות של יבחושין הקליפה משחרת מבחוץ, וכשמסירין הקליפה נשארים היבחושין תחתיה — אין לאוסרן; ולא מתסרי משום "השרץ השורץ על הארץ", כל זמן שלא ריחשה. וגם בקונטרס פי' לעיל גבי "קישות שהתליעה באביה אסורה": כיון דמהלכת התולעת בתוך הקישות והיא מחוברת בקרקע, הויא כמהלכת על גבי קרקע:
Tosafot on Chullin 67b:5:1.english: The language is also precise, as it teaches: Worms that are in the roots of olive trees - From here Rabbeinu Tam, Rabbeinu Netanel, and Riva infer that the halakha is not in accordance with Shmuel, who said [that] a cucumber that became wormy while still attached [to its parent plant] is forbidden. However, in Halakhot Gedolot and in the She'iltot of Rav Achai, he rules in accordance with Shmuel, based on what Rav Pappa said earlier in our chapter (Chullin 58a): "Learn from Rav Huna regarding that which Shmuel said, 'A cucumber that became wormy while still attached is forbidden,' [that] those dates in a jar are permitted after twelve months." Even though the Talmud here draws an inference from the baraita not in accordance with Shmuel, that is [only] at first glance; but according to Shmuel as well, one can resolve and explain that "worms that are in the roots of olive trees" means [worms] that are in the olives while they are still attached to their roots. Nevertheless, even according to Shmuel, one should not forbid those beans that are called pois [peas] in the vernacular, and chickpeas that are called shavim, when [insects] such as yavchushin [gnats] are found inside them — and at the beginning of the formation of yavchushin, the skin turns black on the outside, and when one removes the skin, the yavchushin remain underneath it — one should not forbid them; and they are not forbidden on account of "the swarming thing that swarms upon the earth," as long as it has not crawled [out]. And Rashi also explained earlier regarding "a cucumber that became wormy while still attached is forbidden": since the worm walks inside the cucumber while it is attached to the ground, it is like [a worm] walking on the ground:

Tosafot on Chullin 67b:8:1.hebrew: קוקיאני אסירי - פי' הקונטרס: תולעים שבכבד ושבריאה. וקשיא לר"ת, דלאידך לישנא דשרי, תקשי ליה מברייתא דבסמוך, ד"ואת נבלתם תשקצו" — לרבות דרנים שבבהמה, אע"ג דמינה קא גדלי! אלא אומר ר"ת דבדגים איירי הכא. והא דאמר "כי ניים עייל ליה באוסיא", אשכחן בדגים כי האי גוונא בפ' המוכר את הספינה (ב"ב דף עג:), דאמר רבה בר בר חנה: חזינא ההוא כוורא דיתבה ועיילא ליה טינא באוסייה:
Tosafot on Chullin 67b:8:1.english: Kukeyanei are forbidden - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: worms that are in the liver and in the lung. And this is difficult for Rabbeinu Tam: for according to the other version, which permits [them], there is a difficulty for him from the baraita just below, that [the verse] "And their carcasses you shall have in detestation" [comes] to include worms that are in an animal, even though they grow from [within] it! Rather, Rabbeinu Tam says that [the Gemara] is speaking here about fish. And [as for] that which [the Gemara] says, "When it sleeps, [worms] enter it through its nostril," we find a similar thing with fish in the chapter [entitled] Hamocher et HaSefinah (Bava Batra 73b), where Rabbah bar bar Ḥanah says: I saw a certain fish that was resting, and mud entered its nostril:
